name: GLMdenoise
summary: Denoises task fMRI runs with the GLMdenoise toolbox (compiled MATLAB), deriving PCA noise regressors across runs from BIDS events.tsv designs, and outputs denoised BOLD runs.
description: Builds a design matrix from each run's events.tsv (onset, duration, trial_type), assumes a canonical HRF at the data TR, and runs GLMdenoisedata, which uses cross-validated PCA noise regressors to increase signal-to-noise for task-related voxels. Use it on event-related task fMRI with conditions repeated across at least two runs. Each run needs its own events.tsv; the GLM results are saved to results.mat.

inputs.description: fMRI runs must have conditions repeated across runs. Must have an events.tsv associated with each run specifying onset times and durations of stimuli

outputs.description: Denoised BOLD of the first run (bold.nii.gz, float32) with its events.tsv; further runs are written to denoised_bold/run.

citations.text: Kay K, Rokem A, Winawer J, Dougherty R, Wandell B. GLMdenoise: a fast, automated technique for denoising task-based fMRI data. Front Neurosci 7:247 (2013).
Charest I, Kriegeskorte N, Kay KN. GLMdenoise improves multivariate pattern analysis of fMRI data. NeuroImage 183:606-616 (2018).
Avesani P, et al. The open diffusion data derivatives, brain data upcycling via integrated publishing of derivatives and reproducible open cloud services. Sci Data 6:69 (2019).

failure_modes.message: Must input at least two tfMRI runs with conditions repeated for the cross-validation and noise regression
failure_modes.cause: Only one fMRI run was given.
failure_modes.fix: Provide two or more runs with repeated conditions.

failure_modes.message: fMRI runs must have an events.tsv file associated with it
failure_modes.cause: The number of events.tsv files differs from the number of runs.
failure_modes.fix: Attach an events.tsv to every run.
